## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

The probe inspects item embeddings and sequence-conditioned positive/negative scores through a model-view interface. The underlying trained network is accessed as `view.model`; `view.item_emb` exposes its embeddings. Backbone and readout code are not supplied, so the final user representation cannot be verified here. `log2feats(sequence)` supplies position-level features; any final readout must respect left padding and use the final nonpadding position.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` stores the view and its `meta_data`, `review_data`, and `user_train`; only metadata is subsequently queried. `run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)` invokes two probes. Loader batches contain `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` tensors shaped B × L.

For margins, the probe switches to evaluation mode, calls `log2feats`, stacks positive/negative IDs into B × L × 2 candidates, and calls `predict_score(features, items)`. Positions with positive ID zero are excluded. Computation runs without gradients.

# Probes & Metrics

- **`embedding_collapse_score`:** Samples at most 2,048 real-item embeddings with seed 42, excluding padding/reserved tokens. It normalizes vectors, averages off-diagonal cosine similarities, and maps the mean using `(mean + 1)/2`. Higher values suggest directional collapse; approximately 0.5 means average cosine similarity near zero.
- **`pos_neg_margin_mean` / `pos_neg_margin_p10`:** Mean and lower tenth-percentile positive-minus-negative logits across up to ten batches. Higher values indicate stronger sampled-pair separation.
- **`pos_neg_neg_beats_pos_rate`:** Fraction with negative margins; lower is better.
- **`pos_neg_small_margin_rate`:** Fraction with margins below 0.5; lower indicates fewer weakly separated pairs.
- **`pos_neg_margin_category_breakdown`:** Counts low-margin and wrong-rank positions, plus the twenty most frequent metadata categories for their positive and negative items separately.

# Perturbation & Tests

No sequence perturbation, shuffling, or sensitivity test is performed. Randomness only selects embeddings for the collapse estimate; margins use loader-provided negatives.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

The raw result contains `metrics` and `metric_definitions`. `diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis)` embeds both into a prompt requesting JSON with `status`, `core_findings`, `key_implications`, and `evidence`; it does not itself generate that interpretation.

These probes measure training-pair separation, not validation HR@10, temporal sensitivity, or simulator traits. Margins depend on score scale and negative sampling. Category lists will be empty under this task’s unavailable category metadata, although position totals remain meaningful. Empty valid samples return zeros, potentially obscuring missing evidence. Evaluation mode is not restored afterward.

Recent evidence supports auditing ranking failures beyond sampled-pair margins. [Prakash et al. (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) show that aggregate sequential-recommendation metrics conceal substantial head/mid/tail differences: random negative sampling favors head items, while popularity-based sampling can improve balance at an overall accuracy cost. [Subbiah et al. (2024)](https://research.google/pubs/improved-estimation-of-ranks-for-learning-item-recommenders-with-negative-sampling/) demonstrate benefits from correcting sampled rank estimates for WARP/LambdaRank training. [Dallmann et al. (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.05398) distinguish evaluation resolution, fidelity to full evaluation, robustness to exposure bias, and predictive power. Foundational work establishes that sampled metrics can reverse model comparisons even in expectation ([Krichene and Rendle, 2020](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)).

Practical inference for this task: construct supplementary audits entirely within training histories, withholding a next item from its prefix and excluding that target from model input. Freeze 99 unique negatives per case, seed, eligibility rules, and tie handling across comparisons. Report target rank, HR@10, and boundary margin Δ = target score minus the tenth-highest negative score; positive Δ indicates a hit absent ties. Stratify by prefix length and target frequency computed from training data, reporting user counts, case counts, hits, and user-level bootstrap intervals; resample users together when they contribute multiple prefixes. On an affordable fixed subset, compare sampled and full-catalog ranks and hit/miss disagreements using identical eligibility rules. These are proposed diagnostic implementations, not a standardized protocol established by the cited papers. Full-catalog discrepancies explain failure modes; the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10 remains the selection objective.

Compare the live model with a freshly reconstructed checkpoint and the generated predictor, including item mappings, architecture settings, features and scores; PyTorch recommends saving `state_dict` and calling `eval()` for inference ([serialization guide](https://docs.pytorch.org/tutorials/beginner/saving_loading_models)). Calibrate absolute/relative error against repeated identical runs, then characterize batch-shape changes separately: PyTorch warns that batched and sliced computations need not be bitwise identical ([numerical accuracy](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/notes/numerical_accuracy.html)). Report nonfinite values, maximum errors and top-10 changes rather than simply widening tolerance. Following [DeepMutation’s](https://lilicoding.github.io/papers/ma2018deepmutation.pdf) sensitivity-testing principle, inject isolated diagnostic-only faults: unmasked padding updates, `count-1` readout, cached hidden state, and omitted checkpoint parameters. Require targeted probes to detect them; record undetected mutants without claiming the suite proves correctness.
